chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam, through his chain, elevates it to Abban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

A time will come over the people in which a 'sabta' will befall them, in which knowledge will be bound/restrained as a snake is bound/restrained in its hole. While they are in such a condition, a star will shine to them. I said: 'What is the sabta?' He said: 'The period (of occultation/absence).' I said: 'So what should we do in between that?' He said: 'Remain upon what you are upon until Allah makes your star shine to you.'

key_terms.الْفِتْرَةُ: The period of absence or occultation (ghaybah)
key_terms.سَبْطَةٌ: A period of restraint or hiding, often referring to the occultation of the Imam
key_terms.نَجْمٌ: Star, metaphorically referring to the Imam or a sign of guidance
key_terms.يُأْرَزُ: To be bound, restrained, or confined (like a snake in a hole)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'sabta' and how should believers act during the period of occultation?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (as), the term 'subta' is clarified as a period of 'fitra' (interruption or occultation) where religious knowledge becomes scarce and concealed like a snake in its hole. The Imam advises believers to remain steadfast in their established faith and practice during this interval of uncertainty, awaiting the emergence of their specific 'star' (the Mahdi) as the sign of divine guidance's return.
